### 13:10 to 13:50, a fault of E2's pass at the horizon, and its cure (the limb hold)
- Seen on dive frames 2445 to 2453 and growing through the rise from 2690: a dark line along the horizon, between the ground and the haze of the picture (8 pixels high at 2447).
- Why. The camera of the place window is above the twin, so its limb lies beyond the horizon of the picture. A sky ray between the two was below the twin's horizon, so the pass called it unseen (weight 0) and the globe's own sky showed: dark, with stars, where the close view has its bright dust haze. The ground between the twin's horizon and the limb (one to a few pixels, foreshortened) had no weight either.
- The picture's horizon itself (dumps `out/work/e4/matte/f2454-dump-image.png`, `-alpha.png`): haze meets haze near window row 540, no relief stands above the horizon row, the far mesas start 20 to 55 texels below it. So the row of the horizon may be reused freely.
- The cure, in `src/core/place.ts` (LAY and its mirror `placeUv`), three parts, all off when the reach is 0:
  1. Sky lift. `gap` = the camera's dip minus the twin's dip in the direction of the pixel (`uLimb`: camera up minus twin up, and the difference of the two sines). A sky pixel `own` above the limb looks the picture up `gap * (1 - smoothstep(0, 1, own / max(reach, 2 |gap|)))` higher along the twin's up: at the limb it reads the picture's horizon, at the reach it reads where the twin saw it. Symmetric: a camera below the twin squeezes. The weight of a sky pixel is then whole (`honest` 1).
  2. Ground clamp and hold band. A hit point beyond the twin's horizon looks up the horizon row of the picture at its own azimuth. `hold = 1 - smoothstep(limbHoldDeg[0], limbHoldDeg[1], angle under the limb)` and the weight is at least place weight times the edges times `hold`, so the band under the limb keeps the picture where `seen` and `maxEnlarge` would drop it.
  3. Derivatives. A lifted sky pixel and a clamped ground pixel take the size of a pixel in the picture from the algebra of a direction (`placeSkyGrad` is the mirror), not from `dFdx` and `dFdy`. Why: on the limb a 2 by 2 block holds sky and ground, the picture coordinate jumps inside it (16 texels at 2447), the smaller singular value of that false Jacobian falls under the `maxEnlarge` limit and the pixel loses its weight. Seen as single dark pixels at the stair corners of the limb in the dive (2447: 1421,310 and 1787,314) and as a dashed dark line in the rise (2696, x 1485 to 1900).
- Numbers: `config.handover.place.limbReachDeg` 0 (off film wide) and `limbHoldDeg` [0.25, 0.75]; a stop turns it on per kind with `handover: { dive: { place: { limbReachDeg: 8 } } }` and may give its own `limbHoldDeg`. Mars has 8 on both kinds, from `src/stops/mars/place.json` with a `limbNote`. Harness option `limb=DEG` on the diag string overrides the stop.
- Why off by default: a body without air has stars down to its horizon in both views, so there is nothing dark in the gap, and the lift would move the picture's stars against the globe's own (double stars near the limb). It is for a close view whose horizon carries a haze the globe side does not draw.
- Measured (draft, uncommitted tree then the commit): frame 2447 with `beauty/limb=0` has the bytes of the frame cached before the change (sha256 ba23180d3b60); with the hold no pixel within the limb rows is more than 25 levels darker than both its neighbours on 2447, 2696, 2700 (the test found 60 before on 2447, 198 on 2696). Pictures: `out/work/e4/limb/f2447-three-crop.png` (before, lift only, lift and hold), `f2696-hold-crop.png` (dashes) and `f2696-hold2-crop.png` (cured), `f2700-hold2-strip.png`.
- What it does not cure: in the rise the far field of the picture is cut by `maxEnlarge` 1.2 from 2692 on, so below the held band the globe's own ground shows, plain red brown until the plates agree with the picture. At 2700 the haze stands as a bright band on the right part of the limb (the Sun's side of the close view's sky), at weight 0.43.
- Also seen, not mine: frame 2444, a dark region with a straight edge from the right end of the limb down to the bottom edge. It is in the frame cached before the change too and the place weight there is 0.09: it is a level edge of the old Mars globe, replaced by the ladder of mars_place_builder.

To do after M3, off by default.

### 15:00 to 15:20, edgeIn: the picture comes in from the place outward
- The fault: the pass weights the whole picture by one number in time, so wherever the ground under it is not quite the same ground the picture's sides show as straight lines (its field ends 0.06 of the width right of the frame on Mars).

### 16:50 to 17:10, the tone split (`toneIn`)
- Idea: the picture is split in two. Its detail comes in as before (weight by time, edgeIn). Its broad tone (a wide blur of the frame) is the globe's own near the sides of the picture and the picture's only toward its middle, over a feather far wider than the detail's. The island of fault (a) is the picture's broad tone ending at the feather of the detail; with the tone on its own wide feather there is no rim to see.
- Simulation first, in numpy on rendered draft frames of 4f7b2dd2 (`/tmp/tone/sim.py`, `sim2.py`, `sim3.py`; F from the E4 frames, plates alone with `beauty/noplace`, the weight with `beauty/mask`): with the whole tone taken from the plates the island is gone at a blur of 24, 48 and 96 px; a weight by time alone (tone following the weight) does not help the rise, because at 2694 to 2696 the weight is still 0.97 to 0.82 while the side of the picture is already inside the frame. So the feather is in space: reach = share times (1 minus weight) to a power times the frame. With the power 0.5 the reach opens at a steady speed from T (the weight leaves 1 with a square).
- Engine (`src/core/place.ts`): `toneReach(place, layout)`, `toneGrid(width, height)`, a second shader `lay(true)` (the first, `lay(false)`, is the shader as it was, character for character; a test takes the additions out again and compares), a blur shader. Per sample, only when a reach is above 0: mode 4 writes per cell of 8 frame pixels the frame under the picture (16 taps) times how far the picture counts there (its weight over the weight by time) and that share; mode 5 the same of the picture; each is blurred along both axes (sigma `toneReach` of the frame's height); then the picture is laid with `lent = 1 minus the wide feather`: where the globe's broad tone is the lighter the picture is lifted by `lent` times the difference, where it is the darker the picture is scaled by the ratio (which can not go under zero and keeps the hue).
- A first form that only added the difference turned the limb glow teal at the right edge of 2696 (red pushed under zero where the picture's haze is far brighter than the globe). The lift and scale form has none of it.
- Numbers: `handover.place.toneIn` (four shares, default all 0: off), `tonePower` 0.5, `toneReach` 0.045, `toneCell` 8, checked in `src/config.ts`. Per stop and kind: `place: { toneIn: [left, right, bottom, top] }`. Harness: `tone=L,R,B,T` on the diag string.
- At T the weight is 1, every reach is 0 and the pass is the first shader: the two sides stay equal. While no stop asks, the second shader is never compiled.

### 17:58 to 18:40, E6: the capped shutter (MAIL 310 and 313, decision d129)

- Asked: in the dives and rises of a stop that opted in the shutter of a frame is scaled by `k = min(1, allowed / raw)` around the middle of the full shutter (`raw` as `framePlan` measures it, the larger of both sides in the dissolve frame); keys `handover.maxBlurPx` (6) and `handover.blurEaseFrames` (12); nothing may step at a seam; everything else keeps its bytes; the report prints and judges; unit tests. The rounds of the critics wait for it.
- The ease is my form, agreed in MAIL 313: the blur a frame may keep rises from `maxBlurPx` to the raw motion of the segment's own first or last frame over `blurEaseFrames` (smooth ramp), only where that frame moves more than `maxBlurPx`. That frame then keeps its full shutter (scale exactly 1) beside a neighbour that always ran the full shutter. Where the seam moves less the cap lets go by itself: no ramp. Today one seam needs it: Uranus dive 4199 (10.04 px, terrain 4200 has 9.64), ease frames 4188 to 4199.
- One step beyond the letter of `allowed / raw` (told /root): where a move starts or ends inside the shutter the motion is not even across it, and `allowed / raw` alone left up to 3.6 percent more than allowed (Mercury 990: 6.217 px, Mars 2692: 6.024). The share is therefore corrected twice by the motion measured across the shortened shutter itself (`REFINE` in `src/core/motion.ts`); the motion left then equals the allowed one to 2.4e-6 relative at every capped frame of the film.
- Measured with the cap at 6 (`out/work/handover/e6-STOP-path.md`, written by `npm run handover -- --stop STOP --only path --name e6-STOP-path`; capped frames, least share of the shutter and its frame, most motion across the full shutter, review samples of the segment before and now):

  - mercury.dive 63 of 90, 0.0838 at 737, 71.64 px, 5341 to 1440. mercury.rise 48 of 75, 0.0666 at 1003, 90.23 px, 4871 to 1200.
  - earth.dive 72 of 90, 0.1455 at 1882, 41.24 px, 3862 to 1440. earth.rise 58 of 75, 0.1092 at 2133, 54.94 px, 3830 to 1200.

- An addition to the answer on the rim (sent 19:00, low priority, nothing built): what the eye bridges is blur against step, and that ratio is the same everywhere in the frame: blur / step = 0.5 times the share of the shutter. A film camera runs a share of 1 (180 degrees) down to about 0.25 (45 degrees, the staccato look, still read as motion). With `maxBlurPx` 6 the fastest frames run 0.041 (Mars 2440), 0.067 (Mercury 1003), 0.075 (Uranus 4186), 0.146 (Earth 1882); with 14 Mars 2440 runs 0.095. The knob that answers a strobe directly is a floor on the share: one key (for instance `handover.minShutter`, 0 for off) and `scale = max(allowed / raw, floor)` beside the cap. Because the motion is radial that gives a sharp middle and a streaked rim: with a floor of 0.25 Mars 2440 keeps 4.6 px inside the middle quarter, 12 px inside the middle half, 37 px at the corner; Earth 1882 keeps 2, 4.5 and 10 px. The review tier then needs up to 62 samples in the fastest Mars frames (37 / 0.6), 16 now, 128 before E6. The cap measured over a middle region is the other form (about 30 lines, the probe of `rawMotion` reports every grid point); both can stand side by side: `scale = max(min(1, allowed / rawOfTheRegion), floor)`. /root decides on its clips; do not build before.

- The design (`limbSky`): the pass draws `under * (1 - k) + k * (sky * (1 - A) + RGB)`. Today k for the picture's sky is the weight of the picture times its side feathers, so the horizon of the picture leaves with the picture (and first, with edgeIn at the top). With `limbSky` the rays that miss the ball take `h = max(weight of the picture, share of the close view's sky)` and nothing else: no sides, no limits of enlargement, no land matte. (The first version, 9f850d9, gave the band just under the limb, `limbHoldDeg`, the same weight and clamped the uv of a ray that leaves the picture; both were dropped at 21:24, see the next section.) The share of the close view's sky is the clock on which the two star layers already cross, so the limb of the globe, the haze over it and the stars behind it change as one thing over `skyFrames` (or the stop's own `skyShare`) and reach the picture's values at T.

### 21:15 to 21:30, `limbSky` first try judged, the second version (c148dd1): the sky alone, the side turn

- First try (9f850d9) on Mars, ninth bake, draft, rise 2690 to 2716 (`/tmp/hz/m9/rise-off/`, `/tmp/hz/m9/rise-on/`; sheets `c-rise-off-L1.png`, `c-rise-on-L1.png`, `c-rise-on-L2.png`, `s-rise-on-a.png` in looks at 21:23). Off: the globe's hard bright limb line comes in under the haze from 2695 at the left and is a clear line by 2697. On: the haze stays on the clock of the sky and the line is far fainter, but a dark stripe lies under the limb at 2698 to 2704. It is the picture's own horizon row, held in the band under the limb (`limbHoldDeg`) at the weight of the horizon, on the globe's lit ground. Decision: only the rays that miss the ball take the weight of the horizon. The ground, the band under the limb too, keeps the weight the picture gives it.
- The side turn. The limb is a curve in the picture (on Mars about 2 px per degree of azimuth beyond a side), so a ray of the sky outside a side cannot read the nearest texel: a plain clamp of uv would read ground above the limb. In the second version such a ray (and one that looks away from the picture) is turned about the line to the centre of the body, in the frame of the twin, until it meets the nearer side plane of the picture at its own height over the twin's level; of the two crossings the one in front is taken. Then uv is clamped by half a texel, so over the top it reads the top row. `horizonUv(g, proj, ray, size)` in place.ts is the JS mirror of the shader's `VEIL_SIDE`; `placeUv` now also returns `dir`.
- How often a ray of the sky leaves the picture (`/tmp/hz/uvspan.ts STOP [REACH]`, rays 0.5 and 2 degrees over the limb across the frame, over the whole clock of the sky): Mars never (u 0.08 to 0.89, v 0.64 to 0.70, dive and rise); Mercury dive 722 and 724 a few (worst 1.2 degrees at h 0.08); Earth (skyFrames 120, horizon weight from 1830, limb in frame from about 1882) and Uranus none; Jupiter dive: the limb is above the top of the frame near T (rows minus 298 to minus 389), so no sky in frame there.

### 21:30 to 22:25, `limbSky` third step: the lap of the ball, told by the depth of the frame (bd87601), MAIL 349

- MAIL 349 (21:43): the shutter test of tests/shutter.test.ts fixed and pushed alone (84544e5, head cbb31e6), reported 21:42.
- The second version (c148dd1) left a bright line of 1 to 2 px on the limb in the rise 2696 to 2704: the mesh of the globe (`SphereGeometry(1, seg, seg / 2)`, flat cells) lies inside its sphere by 0 to (pi / seg) squared radii (9.64e-5 for seg 320: 1.2 px at 2699 in mid frame, up to 2 px at the sides), so a ray that meets the sphere there finds no mesh, the pass takes it for ground and the globe's own sky, brightest on the limb, shows. Other meshes: `globe.ts` seg 192, `moonbody.ts` seg 448, Venus circumscribed.
- A plain lap (`handover.place.limbLap`, 0.0001, in radii; a ray whose b * b - c is not above r * r * lap * (2 - lap) is sky) takes the bright line away but leaves darker dashes: where the mesh IS there inside the lap, the picture's dark horizon row is laid at the weight of the sky on the globe's lit ground. No single number cures both: lap 0.00005 left 759 bright columns, 0.0002 gave 233 dark ones (2699).
- So the pass asks the frame who drew the pixel. The veil pass is drawn twice with complementary depth tests, each pixel once: `EqualDepth` (nobody wrote depth: the lap under the sphere is sky, `uVeil.y = max(lap, 0)`), then `NotEqualDepth` (something wrote depth: ground, `uVeil.y = min(lap, 0)`). The veil shader writes `gl_FragDepth = 1.0` (in VEIL_WEIGHT, before the first return and the discard). With lap 0 one draw as before. JS mirror `lapOf(g, drawn)`, `placeUv(g, proj, ray, drawn)`, `horizonUv(..., drawn)`. A globe that writes no depth (Jupiter `globe.ts`, Mercury, the Uranus deck) is sky throughout its lap: it sets `limbLap: 0` or lives with it. In the tone split path only the last draw is tested.

- Brandon's second note (about 21:50, on main 291a78b played live): lag at the change of view on Mercury, Venus, Earth, Jupiter; Mars "zooms in on a flat part of the planet, and then the actual landscape comes in"; Neptune "appears all of a sudden". Section "Second review note of 2026-11-23" in kit/PROGRESS.md on main 1ce3137 (plans E to I).
- What the code does today (read 22:20): `descent(time)` in moves.ts is, before T, `glide(far = the hold going on, low = coast of the close pose at T, share = trapeze(x, rise, fall), turn = trapeze(x, turnRise, turnFall))` with x from the segment's start to T, and after T `twin(diveTerrain(time))`, the close view's own entry (offset times g = x to the power 2.2). Three laws: the trapeze, the coast (tanh over coastFrames), the entry. The log height rate dents at T because the trapeze falls to the close pose's own rate at T and the entry then speeds up again. The rise is the mirror (`ascent`, exit offsets with g, `fromDive`).
- The report's rate is `log(prev.height / height)` per frame at mid shutter on the frame's side (tools/handover.ts 340), its mean so far over the far part only.
- Design sent to /root at 22:30 (and what was promised, see Next). E: one glide over the WHOLE segment between the hold going on and the surface view's own move carried back from its first frame at its own velocity (the coast anchored at the segment's end), one share for height, direction, attitude and field, its rate one bell with zero at both ends and flanks of bounded slope; the close view is drawn from the same eye through the inverse of the twin; entry and exit offsets, turnRise, turnFall, fromDive, coastFrames retire (fields stay in the type). F: a switch per stop `handover.scene`: "views" (today), "globe" (the globe side holds the close ground, the engine draws the orbit group alone from hold to travel, surface view through the twin, no T), "both" (the engine draws the terrain group through the twin into a layer, border by distance on the ground, depth against the far scene); one air (exposure, sky, limb, haze, Sun) as a curve over log height.
- The bell (decided, not coded): rate r(x) = P * S(x / a) on the rise flank, P on the plateau, P * S((1 - x) / b) on the fall, P = 1 / (1 - (a + b) / 2); S is the S curve with corner share j: S'(u) = min(u / j, 1, (1 - u) / j) / (1 - j). Its integral A(u): u <= j: u^3 / (6 j (1 - j)); j..1-j: j^2 / (6 (1 - j)) + (u - j) u / (2 (1 - j)); above: A(1 - j) + (u - (1 - j)) - (j^3 - (1 - u)^3) / (6 j (1 - j)); A(1) = 1/2. Share: P a A(x / a); P (a / 2 + x - a); 1 - P b A((1 - x) / b). Largest step of the rate per frame over the mean: P / ((1 - j) min(a, b) N) for N frames (a = b = 0.5, j = 0.25: 0.059 for 90 frames, 0.071 for 75).
- The step at Saturn 3832 (read, not reproduced): `rawMotion` is the largest of a 17 by 9 grid of tracked points; in the terrain view only rays under the horizon are tracked (the ground plane), points behind the eye at one end of the shutter are dropped, so the measure steps (18.5 to 21.9 px) and the share with it (0.759 to 0.640); the REFINE loop repeats it. Cure planned: track every ray always (sky rays at infinity, points held at the rim of a bounded field), and the share at a film position p as a weighted mean of the shares at fixed nodes in time under a smooth window.

### 05:02 to 05:35 (24 Nov), the bend: an engine option off by default, the seam tool's advice, Mars bends on its own

- WHAT THE DENT IS, in one line: the surface view ends pushing forward and down; the one move alone leaves the seam back and up (on main's Mars 161 degrees from the view's way, on Mars's own tree 169), so the eye stops and turns round. The cure is a surface view that ends on a way the move can take without a stop.
- THE ENGINE OPTION (in the commit that holds this line, off by default, no stop of the film names it): `src/director/bend.ts`, class `Bend(start, shape)`: from where it begins the eye keeps the share of its height it flies a second (so the near ground never slows) and the direction of its way turns in one plane, from its own way toward `acrossDeg` ([azimuth, elevation]: azimuth in the ground's level plane from the level part of the way, 90 to the right, 270 to the left; elevation above it) by `turnDeg`, on a smooth step (rest to rest, so no corner at the start and a straight line at the end). The place is a sum by a fourth order step at fixed nodes (`handover.carry.stepsPerFrame` a film frame), so the eye at a time does not depend on what was asked before. Nothing in it knows a frame number. `MoveParams.terrain.bend = { frames, acrossDeg, turnDeg }` puts it on the last `frames` film frames of the engine's surface view (the lens stays the straight path's own); a stop with a path of its own can build a `Bend` itself (`plan.closeGround(position, time)` gives the ground's up and the height in the close view's frame, through the twin and back).
- `plan.eyeFirstWay(kind)`: the way the one move alone takes the eye from the seam with the surface view at rest (unit vector, close view's frame). `tools/seam.ts` prints under a rise on the one move where the move alone leaves the seam and the `acrossDeg`, `turnDeg` of the bend that ends on it. `eyeOrbit` was split for it (`eyeGlide`, same operations in the same order).
- MEASURED on main's Mars with the option set in memory (scratch `out/work/tmp/bendcheck.ts`; 60 frames): acrossDeg [70.1, 45.3] turnDeg 161.2 (the plane the tool names): lowest 1.050 at 2670, never against the way, the view's largest step 0.006, judge green. [90, 0] 161.2: 1.051, green. [90, 0] 180: 1.050. [270, 0] 161.2: 1.044. 45 frames 1.046, 30 frames 1.042. ### 10:00 to 10:20 (24 Nov), 2(b) AS BUILT: the engine's sky weight and place weight by the height of the eye

- WHAT IT IS (`src/director/handover.ts`): `skyWeight(seg, time)` and `placeWeight(seg, time)` keep their signatures (Earth's set calls `skyWeight` and divides it out against its own law). Between the far end of a span and T each is `smooth(base + (1 - base) * (ln far - ln h) / (ln far - ln near))`: h the height of the globe camera over the unit sphere at the sample's time, far the height at the time the span begins (sky: `full` less `skyFrames / fps` in a dive, plus it in a rise, cut to the segment; picture: `placeFirstFrame / fps` in a dive, `(placeLastFrame + 1) / fps` in a rise), near the height at `full` (`firstFrame / fps` in a dive, `(lastFrame + 1) / fps` in a rise), base the clock's value at the far end (0, or what the clock had where the segment cuts the span: Earth, 0.166 and 0.34). THE COST AND THE CACHE: built first with no cache at all (far and near asked at every call; an `eyeShot(kind, time, 'orbit')` costs 2 to 15 microseconds, `out/work/tmp/eyecost.ts`), and the first whole chain went red on it: `tests/shutter.test.ts` (the sample count under the floor of the share) ran 6.7 s against 3.2 s and hit the 5 s limit, `tests/near.test.ts` 7.1 s against 4.8 s, the frame plan test of `tests/handover.test.ts` 2.8 s against 1.2 s. Measured (`out/work/tmp/shotcost.ts`): `skyWeight` 24 microseconds and `placeWeight` 16 a call on Mars's dive, three poses each, about as much again as the rest of a shot. AS BUILT NOW: the two ends of a span are asked once for a film and kept with its eye (`spanEnds`, a WeakMap by the eye function the film registers; key: segment id, far time, near time, the forced one move, the count of handover changes), and the film asks the height of the sample once for both weights (`eyeHeightAt`, passed as the optional third argument of `skyWeight` and `placeWeight`). A film is made for the paths its plans have when it is made (its legs are read once, too), so the ends can only go stale where a test changes a path under a living film without a new plan or the forced one move; none does. The shot dumps of the cached build equal the uncached ones by sha256 at both rates (`after2-1.txt`, `after2-2.txt`). The seven tests that make the plan of every frame of every dive and rise got a limit of 60 s (`LONG` in `tests/shutter.test.ts`, `tests/handover.test.ts`, `tests/pace.test.ts`): they ran 2.5 to 3.8 s of the 5 s before this already.

- DESIGN B, AS BUILT: THE FAR END COMES OUT. `handover.rise.pullBack: { speed, over }` in a stop's own params (`HandoverSide.pullBack` in handover.ts; speed in radii a second above the drift at the end of the rise, over in seconds). `StopPlan.pullBack(time)` in moves.ts: how far the far end of the rise stands back along the line of the exit (`riseOut`), in radii: s = min((rise.end - time) / over, 1), back = speed over (s - s^3 + s^4 / 2). So before the last `over` seconds the far end stands back by speed over / 2 and drifts as before; in the last `over` seconds its excess over the drift comes in as the smooth step 1 - 3 s^2 + 2 s^3 (no step in speed or acceleration where it leaves the drift, acceleration 0 at the end), and it reaches the end pose at drift + speed. `after(time)` is `exitPose(time)` less that (the hold where the rise goes into one). The rise comes to rest on its far end as it always did, so the eye ends on `riseEnd` and flies drift + speed along the drift's own line; the turn and the angle of view are the end pose's, untouched. Every path that glides onto `after(time)` gets it, the one move and a stop's own alike. WITHOUT THE OPTION `pullBack` returns 0 and `after` does not touch the pose: to the bit. - WHAT IT IS: a pixel of a frame is laid over the frame before by the ground it shows (its ray to the unit sphere of the body, back by this frame's turn of the body, forward by the turn of the frame before, projected into that frame, read between its pixels). Ground the frame before does not show is NEW ground: counted as a share, left out of the change. The rim of the body, one pixel in either frame, holds sky and is left out (without that a synthetic rise read +0.80 where the truth is 0). A frame gets: `seen` (share of the body whose ground the frame before shows), `level` and `colour` (mean change on it, signed), `rms`, `fresh` (level of the new ground), `kept` (level of the ground seen in both).
- THE CONVENTION, proven on real pictures (`/tmp/law/ip/proto.py`): ground = turn(now) inverse times the point, then turn(before). Close view of Jupiter 3241 to 3268: rms 4 to 5 that way, 33 to 45 without the turn or with it reversed.

So the direction of the way at a fragment is `b.xy / b.w - a.xy / a.w`, x right and y up as dFdx and dFdy. With the unit way (wx, wy): along = dx * wx + dy * wy, across = dy * wx - dx * wy.

### Design (c), the crests, as it is being built (worktree crest-wt, branch agent/engine-crest on 4bae298b, local only so far)

- src/terrain/crest.ts (pure): crestField(dist, w, h, cell, { step, walk, under }): inverse distance; range in a window of half a
  cell less the least range within a walk (what the ground does anyway) over step makes the zone; the way across is the evened slope;
  from every zone texel a walk both ways to the first even texel gives the near end and the far end (dropped if the walk is too long
  or the ends differ by less than step). Fields: near and far distance (own to the bit on the texel's own side, the end's on the other),
  share (cut at the ramp's middle), the way to the far end, away (texels from the nearest ramp). crestTexels packs share and way into
  bytes; crestCells names the cells: 1 sheets in place of the cell, 2 the far sheet under a near cell (within under), 0 left.
- src/terrain/relief.ts: ReliefMotion.crest?: { layer, step, walk, under }[]. In load the kind 1 cells become one vertex six times in
  the layer's index (no triangle, no mark in the shield) and one more mesh, the sheets, is added after the layer's (same renderOrder,
  later id, so it draws after): far cells first, then near cells; vertices by the mesh's own sampler from the far and near fields.
  The sheets' material has the layer's shaders through withSheets and the layer's uniforms object itself, so update needs nothing;
  presence, edge, law, eye scale and dispose go over skins(l). uCut is a window of the map (uCutBox), uCutMap the map's size and scale.
  The cut in the shader is one pixel soft (fwidth), the far sheet goes over to the far end's texel with the share.
- Order: both sheets AFTER the layer's mesh. Far before the mesh would show through part alpha of near cells from the picture's eye.
- From the picture's eye the picture comes back but for the pixel of the cut (at most a quarter of the far ground's colour there).
- Cells the ridge has a hand in stay in the mesh. Apron cells are never sheets.
- Tests: tests/crest.test.ts (finding, cells, meshes, shaders), tests/crest-gl.test.ts (pixels in the browser). Not yet run at 18:55.
- Open: depth of the far sheet under near cells where the step is small (the stop's step keeps it apart; watch in the frames); the
  colour rule and a cut file are a second step; Mars's numbers are the stop's (trial numbers in scratch only).

  what it was), so the near sheet keeps the painted crest whole and the far sheet shows only the far end's texel there; (ii) the far
  sheet draws its fill only where the layer's own texel is opaque (a gate on the own alpha), so nothing appears outside the matte;

- THE CURE OF DESIGN (c), CODED 19:52 to 20:05 in crest-wt (uncommitted; v1 saved as /tmp/crest/crest.v1.ts, relief.v1.ts,
  crest.test.v1.ts, crest-gl.test.v1.ts). It replaces the plan (i) to (iv) above: the CPU cannot know the matte (SetContext has only
  texture() and buffer()), so the SHADER asks it.
  - crest.ts: a fourth number out (texels of the map the near side's paint reaches beyond the step's middle; left out 0; refused under
    0 or over one cell). The share is now a true distance to the line of the middle (marching squares over the soft middle on ramp
    texels, plus or minus one half on band texels), moved out by out, one texel wide. New fields: side (by PLACE: the side of the
    nearest ramp texel, not by the texel's own distance), toNearX/Y (way to the near end of the nearest ramp texel, for ramp texels
    and band texels within ceil(1.5 cell) + 2; else 0: the texel asks itself). toFar is also set for far side texels within
    ceil(out) + 2 of a ramp, and reads the far ground out texels BEYOND the far end on the line from the near end to the far end (the
    far end is the first even ground and may lie as near to the middle as the cut does). The band is now found by two sweeps that
    hand the nearest ramp texel on (Euclidean), not by a flood over 8 neighbours: the flood gave every band texel a ramp texel along
    a 45 degree diagonal (found by a test of a crest lying flat: the way to the far ground was 2 texels off sideways), so the fill
    under the near side would have run in diagonal streaks. away is now ceil of the true distance. crestTexels gives two arrays
    (cut: share, way to far x, y, 255; back: way to near x, y, 0, 255). crestCells(field, nx, ny, {under, out}): kind 1 also where a
    far side texel beside a ramp is taken by the cut.
  - relief.ts: sampler uCutBack (nearest); aSheet 1 near, 0 far in place of a cell, -1 far under a kept cell (vertices of its own);
    cutGround = step(0.5, matte at the near end); cutOwn = cutShare x cutGround; the near sheet is the layer's texel times cutOwn;
    the far sheet is the layer's texel times (1 - cutOwn) and, under a texel that is opaque within CREST_SOLID (2/255, a named
    exported constant), the far end's texel with the far end's alpha; the under sheet is that fill alone. So: a step whose near side
    is no ground is a rim and rides with the far side; a far side that is no ground draws nothing; nothing under a texel that is
    not opaque.

    cleared colour showed through. RIGHT: cutMine = alpha x mix(1 - cutOwn, cutOwn, cutNear) x (1 - cutUnder); cutLent = cutAlpha x
    cutFill; alpha = cutMine + cutLent; texel = mix(texel, cutTexel, cutLent / max(alpha, 1e-6)): the two parts added as covers,

   mesh that the cut crosses, with the near sheet at the near field and the far sheet at the far field and the mesh's wall between.
   Cure `crestEnds(field, kinds, nx, ny)` in crest.ts: the vertices at both ends of a side between a kind 1 cell and one that is not
   (the map's rim counts as not) along which both grounds are read (a texel with share over `least` and one under 128). At those
   vertices the near sheet and the far sheet take the mesh's own distance. Browser test at eyes 0.5: 0 open pixels (it was 106, 285,
   34, 187 by the earlier session's count, not measured again).

   end from eyes with x = +1. Cause PROVEN: three sorts the transparent meshes of one render order by the depth of the middle of
   their bounds before the id, so from some eyes the sheets were drawn BEFORE the layer's mesh; the near sheet's faint edge
   (alpha just over the discard) wrote depth and shut the mesh's far ground out behind it. Cure: `sheetMesh.renderOrder = k + 0.5`
   (after its layer's mesh, before the next layer's). Measured with it: 0 open at all 8 eyes of 1.0, all 6 cuts.
   The frame of the count at 1.0 needs the corner factor 1 / hypot(1, WIDTH/2/FOCAL, HEIGHT/2/FOCAL) on both axes (the plain mesh
   showed 4, 42, 50 px at the frame's edge with the factor by axis).

   distance (the far end of the cells `under`, the sides of the kind 2 cells beyond a crest's end, the near part of an end side).
   Cure, coded 22:44: `crestRing(kinds, nx, ny)` (a kind 0 cell that touches a kind 1 or 2 cell by a side or a corner becomes 3:
   keeps the mesh, gets the under sheet) and `crestRim(kinds, nx, ny)` (vertices with a kind 0 cell or the map's rim among their
   four). In relief.ts: `kinds = crestRing(crestCells(...))`, then the ridge's taking out, then `ends`, `rim`; `vertex()`:
   near sheet `ends ? own : near field`; far sheet `(ends || rim) ? own : far field`; under sheet the same and at least
   `own * (1 + CREST_BEHIND)`. So the far sheet's rim lies on the ground all round and the rise happens inside the ring cell.
   Known and left: at an end vertex on the near side the far sheet (own) and the under sheet (own times 1.001) differ by a
   thousandth along one side under the near ground; at eyes of 1.0 that is 0.004 px wide at mid side.
4. The near sheet's fold: at an end vertex on the far side the near sheet goes from the near distance to the far one over one cell.
   In the end cell that is the zip (one tooth). In the far side's neighbour cell it is paint with share 0, or within 1.5 px of the
   cut on one unbroken surface; its depth writes hurt only when the sheets were drawn before the mesh (fault two). Left as it is.

## 23:21 to 00:07 UTC, 25 to 26 Nov: the finding rewritten (three rules), D's blob traced to the layer's rim, a box cures it

State: ALL UNCOMMITTED in `crest-wt` (branch agent/engine-crest at b75720ab). Backups of the state before this entry: `/tmp/crest/crest.v7.ts`, `relief.v7.ts`, `crest.test.v7.ts`, `crest-gl.test.v7.ts`.

What changed in `src/terrain/crest.ts` since v7, and why:
1. The finding (23:25). The old finding (zone by the range against the least range within a walk, both ends by the first texel under a threshold) made a false ramp on a steady slope beside a plain (2668: a break at x 733..768 y 712..727 and a dark notch at 765..775, 726..730). New: the way from a texel is walked whole to either side (`wayAt`), an end is where the range falls no further by more than a step as far as the way goes on, and a step counts only by what the two ends differ by, less what ground as even as the two sides would do anyway over the way between them.
2. The top rule (23:40). An end closed on the step itself (far 7.4 percent off at map (1562,383..384): an orange blob at 2668 (690,653) and a jump of 7 px at rows 653..655). Now `top` is the place of the greatest range within a cell along the way, and an end lies at or beyond it.
3. The past rule (23:52). A band texel that lies on along the crest's line past a ramp's end (no way across the nearest ramp texel leads to it to within half a right angle) has no other side: both sheets keep the map's own distance, and the texel is the near side's where its own ground is nearer than the middle of the step at the end. So the cut goes on from an end along the height of the middle, and the sheets lie on the mesh's own surface there.

### 05:00 to 06:18 UTC (26 Nov), THE WORD BOTH on SkyPatch (neptune_builder's ask of 05:00), built on the arrive name, NAMED 06:16

The ask (05:00, high, copy to the Builder by MAIL 1395 ruling 2): one word on SkyPatch, `both?: boolean`. A patch that carries it is drawn in both views of its stop, each at the aim of its own view, with base 1 through dive, terrain and rise; it never goes through skyShare. Why: by ruling 2 of MAIL 1395 Neptune's sky from 4690 to the end of the rise is one set of pictures fixed on the sky, weight 1, the same in both views, and nothing of the sky may change at T (4758.3). Its trial lines came as an attachment (`both-word.txt`): the field, and two conditions in the unshared branch of the engine's loop.

Judged sound, taken as asked (YES went to neptune_builder 05:05, with the branch name and five points on what the engine does and does not do):
- Nothing by the clock (Plan F): base 1 from the dive's first frame to the rise's last.
- Off by default: both conditions are the old ones where the word is absent.
- The aim is already per patch view in the engine (`aims.patches[stop][patch.view]`), so the patch of one view lies at the same place on the sky when the other view draws it. The patch lives in the sky's frame after the turn (`sd = uFrame * dir`, sky.ts), the same frame as the stars; where the stop's carry and turn are whole at T (Neptune's skyCarryShare and skyTurnShare by the eye's height) both views see one sky there.
- The slots: `Sky.setPatches` takes the first two of the list. The unshared branch does not sort, so the order is the set's list in both views; slot B is laid over slot A where both replace (sky.ts `patched`). A third patch above zero is dropped without a word, as before. Neptune's set has two patches (sky.json: orbit, terrain; both replace).
- The stop's `weight(time, view)` is asked with the view of the set that draws, as the unshared branch did (the one case where it differs from the patch's view is the word's).
- Not in a hold, not on a travel: the surface view's patch comes on at the dive's first frame and every patch of the stop goes to 0 at the first frame after the rise. The engine does not check that nothing of them lies in the frame there (the stop answers, as with `arrive`).
- The word is read only in the unshared branch. ON MAIN NEPTUNE SHARES: 39 frames of its dive and 33 of its rise have skyShare above 0 (move.json sky.own true; counted with a scratch test over film.shotAt). - WHAT THE AIM IS (asked by neptune_builder): a stop may give `skyAim.arrive` (three numbers like its orbit aim). Then in the rise of the stop before and on the travel to the stop the sky has the turn of that aim (`FilmDirector.arrivals[id].turn`, read by `turnIn`), the stop's orbit pictures stand by the aim on the travel (`arrivals[id].orbit`) so they keep their place in the lens, and at the first frame of the stop's hold the stars step to the stop's own turn. The engine draws that step only under an orbit picture of the stop that hides the stars (`skyStep` in `src/core/skyfloor.ts`), else it refuses. Refused on the first two stops, on a stop that follows the turn of the stop before, on the stop the sky is fitted on, on a stop with no orbit aim of its own.

## 20:07 to 20:23 UTC, 26 Nov: the merge is red in one test of mine (a tolerance at the floor of the angle measure); cured in a test commit, 7d88f13c; the proofs run again

- THE PROOFS ON THE MERGE e5d49660 (log `/tmp/sun/rp.log`, results kept in `/tmp/sun/rp-e5d49660/`, done 20:19:50): build exit 0; tsc exit 0, 0 lines; the nine path lines exit 0 on the tip and on main 262b9a68 and are the same bytes stop by stop (ALL NINE GREEN on this main: Venus's two rise lines and Saturn's four dive lines of the old main are gone with the fifth cut); cues exit 0, shots exit 0, `cut/` unchanged; the shot dump equal to main's (5400 lines, sha256 starts 4b612d7b779bd76e). THE SUITE: 1117 tests, 1116 passed, 1 FAILED, 96 files: `tests/skyseen.test.ts`, "the count takes in the turn between the two aims", line 191: "expected +0 to be close to 0.0000017075472925031877, received difference is 0.0000017075472925031877, but expected 5e-7".
- THE CAUSE, measured with a scratch copy of the test's helpers (`t-cut/out/work/tmp/seenends.ts`): the test's subject is the last stop with a low aim and no second one: Neptune (index 8, turn span 4854 to 4866, whole turn 72.666 degrees). The sky of the one aim stands still through the surface view; its count from frame to frame is 0 or 1.7075e-6 degrees, which is `2 * acos(1 - 2^-53)`: one unit in the last place of the dot of two quaternions that are equal to the last digit but one. With Neptune's numbers of the fifth cut the still sky of the one aim reads 1.7075e-6 from 4853 to 4854 and the sky of the two aims reads 0 there (the two stand in different attitudes before the span, so their last digits differ). The test compared the two with `toBeCloseTo(x, 6)` (5e-7): under the floor of the measure. On the old main the two happened to read alike. The law in `film.ts` compares the count with the limit of 0.5 degrees and has no such comparison.
- THE CURE, in the test alone: one named floor `STILL = 1e-4` degrees in `tests/skyseen.test.ts` (the value the file's two other angle comparisons already used as a literal); the two ends are compared as `Math.abs(a - b) < STILL`; the lowest limit of the refusal test is taken from the pairs over STILL (it took the least value above 0, which could be a 1.7e-6 of the floor; it passed, but only because the film's count repeats to the last bit). A turn that leaked one frame past its span would read 0.29 degrees there and is still caught. No source file changes.
- COMMIT 7d88f13cc2145f2e371ef3506ad15bee6cca3381 on the merge e5d49660 (local; "Tests: the ends of the seen turn's count are compared above the floor of the angle measure"). The file alone with the cure in `t-cut`: 11 of 11. THE PROOFS RUN AGAIN on 7d88f13c against main 262b9a68 since 20:21:58: log `/tmp/sun/rp2.log`, results `/tmp/sun/rp/`.
- WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE NAME: f7416333 (named 19:44, green on main 60439d8c) would be red by this one test once merged on the fifth cut's main. The name moves to the new sha when its proofs are green; /root is told then in a NAMED mail (MAIL 1314: a merge that changes a stated number is said; MAIL 1473: a red machine check is a bug, no sha goes on with it).
- LESSON: a test that compares two angles each read through `angleTo` must name a floor above 1.7e-6 degrees times a few; `toBeCloseTo` with 6 decimals on degrees is under it.

The tree after it: `git status` 0 lines; free 11972 MB. Kept: `out/work/chunks/16x9-final-full/venus.dive.span1327-1334.mp4` and its `.json` (until /root says they can go).
- A WRONG READING OF MINE, corrected in the return: at 21:26:16 I sent /root the line "the first frame is not written after 15 minutes", because no part file stood under `out/work/tmp/film/`. The part file `venus.dive.part000.mkv` only appears once the encoder (ffmpeg, reading PNG frames from a pipe) has taken in about three frames, and it stays at 0 bytes until the end. The frames in truth came about 324 s apart from the start: the encoder's bytes read (`/proc/PID/io`, rchar) stepped by 4.15 MB at 21:39:11, 21:44:35 and 21:49:59, and 2650 s for 8 frames says the same. No frame took over 15 minutes.
- HOW TO READ A RUNNING JOB: the tool logs only every tenth frame of a part (`tools/film.ts`, line 175) and "wrote" at the end of a part. Between those: `/tmp/jobs/NAME-io.txt`, written by `/tmp/jobs/iowatch2.sh NAME` (each step of rchar of about 4 MB is one frame delivered to the encoder). Final tier, master format, Venus's dive 1327 to 1334: 5.4 minutes a frame on this machine (4 cores, the drawing process at 370 percent of a core, about 2.2 GB of memory).
- HELPERS for the next jobs: write the job's lines exactly as mailed (the mail shows `>` and `&` as `&gt;` and `&amp;`: decode them) to `/tmp/jobs/NAME.sh`, check with `bash -n`, then `bash /tmp/jobs/start.sh NAME` (refuses when a render runs; starts the script detached from the tree's root and the watcher). Finished when `/tmp/jobs/NAME-run.log` holds "SCRIPT DONE".

### `/tmp/jobs/pre.sh` (2079 bytes, 25 lines)

```
# pre.sh NAME : the steps before a job, in order: no render running, the cache dropped with sudo, the clean tree checked
# (HEAD, git status, the lock, free space), the script /tmp/jobs/NAME.sh checked for syntax and against the mailed lines
# (lines 6 to 9 of /tmp/jobs/NAME-mail.txt), npm run build, then the start. Stops at the first thing that is not as it must be.
N=$1
[ -f /tmp/jobs/$N.sh ] && [ -f /tmp/jobs/$N-mail.txt ] || { echo "STOP: script or mail file missing"; exit 1; }
date -u
[ "$(pgrep -f 'tools/film.ts' | wc -l)" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: a render is running"; exit 1; }
bash -n /tmp/jobs/$N.sh || { echo "STOP: syntax"; exit 1; }
[ "$(wc -l < /tmp/jobs/$N.sh)" = 4 ] || { echo "STOP: the script has not 4 lines"; exit 1; }
diff <(sed -n 6,9p /tmp/jobs/$N-mail.txt) /tmp/jobs/$N.sh > /dev/null || { echo "STOP: the script differs from the mailed lines"; exit 1; }
echo "script: syntax ok, 4 lines, equals the mailed lines"
if sudo -n sh -c 'sync; echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'; then echo "DROPPED with sudo at $(date -u +%H:%M:%S)" | tee /tmp/jobs/$N-cache.txt; else echo "NOT DROPPED: sudo does not work" | tee /tmp/jobs/$N-cache.txt; fi
cd /home/user/workspace/master || exit 1
H=$(git rev-parse HEAD); echo "HEAD $H"
[ "$H" = 262b9a68df0a6bda8d77518539580de554bb0dc5 ] || { echo "STOP: HEAD is not 262b9a68"; exit 1; }
[ "$(git status --porcelain | wc -l)" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: git status shows a change"; git status --porcelain | head; exit 1; }
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || { echo "STOP: the lock changed"; exit 1; }
echo "git status 0 lines, lock unchanged"
F=$(df -m / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}'); echo "free before the build: $F MB" | tee /tmp/jobs/$N-free.txt
[ "$F" -ge 4000 ] || { echo "STOP: under 4 GB free"; exit 1; }
npm run build > /tmp/jobs/$N-build.log 2>&1; B=$?; echo "build exit $B"
[ $B = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: build failed"; tail -5 /tmp/jobs/$N-build.log; exit 1; }
[ "$(git status --porcelain | wc -l)" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: git status shows a change after the build"; exit 1; }
bash /tmp/jobs/start.sh $N
date -u
```

```
# start.sh NAME : runs /tmp/jobs/NAME.sh (the job's lines exactly as mailed) detached from the root of the clean tree, with a marker when it has finished.
N=$1
cd /home/user/workspace/master || exit 1
[ -f /tmp/jobs/$N.sh ] || { echo "no script /tmp/jobs/$N.sh"; exit 1; }
pgrep -f 'tools/film.ts' > /dev/null && { echo "a render is running, not started"; exit 2; }
date -u +%T > /tmp/jobs/$N-start.txt
date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S > /tmp/jobs/$N-start-iso.txt
rm -f /tmp/jobs/$N-run.log /tmp/jobs/$N-io.txt
(set -m; (bash /tmp/jobs/$N.sh; echo "SCRIPT DONE $(date -u +%T)") > /tmp/jobs/$N-run.log 2>&1 &)
(set -m; bash /tmp/jobs/iowatch2.sh $N > /dev/null 2>&1 &)
echo "started $N at $(cat /tmp/jobs/$N-start.txt)"
```

### `/tmp/jobs/iowatch2.sh` (507 bytes, 12 lines, 1 sign replaced)

```
# iowatch2.sh NAME : logs the bytes read by the job's encoder (ffmpeg) to /tmp/jobs/NAME-io.txt; each step of about 4 MB is one frame delivered.
N=$1
last=-1
while :; do
  grep -q 'SCRIPT DONE' /tmp/jobs/$N-run.log 2>/dev/null && break
  p=$(pgrep -f 'ffmpeg -hide_banner' | head -1)
  if [ -n "$p" ]; then
    r=$(awk '/^rchar/{print $2}' /proc/$p/io 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$r" ] && [ "$r" NOT_EQUAL_SIGN "$last" ]; then echo "$(date -u +%T) pid $p rchar $r" >> /tmp/jobs/$N-io.txt; last=$r; fi
  fi
  sleep 5
done
```

```
# rows.py SEGMENT FIRST LAST START_ISO : the finished frames of a running job from out/work/looks/log.jsonl of the clean tree
# (one row a finished frame when frames take over ten minutes), with the minutes each took. START_ISO like 2026-11-26T23:24:11
import json, sys, datetime
seg, first, last, start = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4]
t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(start)
rows = []
for l in open('/home/user/workspace/master/out/work/looks/log.jsonl'):
    try:
        r = json.loads(l)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if r.get('segment') NOT_EQUAL_SIGN seg or r.get('job') NOT_EQUAL_SIGN 'film':
        continue
    f = r.get('frame')
    if f is None or f < first or f > last:
        continue
    t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(r['time'][:19])
    if t < t0:
        continue
    rows.append((t, f))
rows.sort()
prev = t0
out = []
for t, f in rows:
    out.append('%d at %s (%.0f min)' % (f, t.strftime('%H:%M:%S'), (t - prev).total_seconds() / 60))
    prev = t
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
print('%d finished: %s; since the last %.0f min' % (len(rows), ', '.join(out) if out else 'none', (now - prev).total_seconds() / 60))
```

```
# mkline.py NAME SEGMENT FIRST LAST START_ISO : prints the line owed to /root while a slow job runs (the frames finished so far
# and the time each took, from the rows of the job in out/work/looks/log.jsonl of the clean tree). Exit 1 when the state is not
# the plain one (the script has finished, or the log holds an error line or an RC line): then write the line by hand.
import json, sys, datetime, re
name, seg, first, last, start = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4]), sys.argv[5]
t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(start)
rows = {}
for l in open('/home/user/workspace/master/out/work/looks/log.jsonl'):
    try:
        r = json.loads(l)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if r.get('segment') NOT_EQUAL_SIGN seg or r.get('job') NOT_EQUAL_SIGN 'film':
        continue
    f = r.get('frame')
    if f is None or f < first or f > last:
        continue
    t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(r['time'][:19])
    if t < t0:
        continue
    rows.setdefault(f, t)
log = open('/tmp/%s-log.txt' % name, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
bad = len(re.findall(r'Shader Error|not usable|FAILED|lost', log))
rc = len(re.findall(r'RC film', log))
try:
    done = 'SCRIPT DONE' in open('/tmp/jobs/%s-run.log' % name).read()
except Exception:
    done = False
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
total = last - first + 1
items = sorted(rows.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
prev = t0
parts = []
for i, (f, t) in enumerate(items):
    m = round((t - prev).total_seconds() / 60)
    if i == 0:
        parts.append('%d at %s (%d minutes from the start at %s, with the load)' % (f, t.strftime('%H:%M:%S'), m, t0.strftime('%H:%M:%S')))
    else:
        parts.append('%d at %s (%d minutes)' % (f, t.strftime('%H:%M:%S'), m))
    prev = t
since = int((now - prev).total_seconds() // 60)
head = 'handover_engineer on JOB %s, %s UTC %s: ' % (name, now.strftime('%H:%M'), now.strftime('%d %b').lstrip('0'))
if items:
    body = '%d of %d frames finished (rows of this job in out/work/looks/log.jsonl): %s. ' % (len(items), total, ', '.join(parts))
    if len(items) < total:
        body += 'The next frame runs since then, %d minutes so far. ' % since
else:
    body = '0 of %d frames finished, %d minutes after the start at %s (no row of this job in out/work/looks/log.jsonl). ' % (total, since, t0.strftime('%H:%M:%S'))
tail = 'The render runs on, no error line and no RC line in the log.'
print(head + body + tail)
if done or bad or rc:
    sys.stderr.write('NOT PLAIN: done %s bad %d rc %d\n' % (done, bad, rc))
    sys.exit(1)
```

```
# mkreturn.py NAME PIECE SEGMENT FIRST LAST : writes the draft of the return mail of a finished job to /tmp/mail/NAME-return.out
# from the files of the job (tail, log, start, cache, run log, tar pieces) and prints it. The line of times ends with the words
# TIMES_NOTE, to be replaced by hand (the speed, slow frames); the list of kept chunks is read from the folder.
import sys, os, re, glob, subprocess, datetime
name, piece, seg, first, last = sys.argv[1:6]
tail = open('/tmp/%s-tail.txt' % name).read().split('\n')
log = open('/tmp/%s-log.txt' % name, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
rcs = [l for l in log.split('\n') if l.startswith('RC film')]
wrote = [l for l in log.split('\n') if l.startswith('wrote ')]
start = open('/tmp/jobs/%s-start.txt' % name).read().strip()
cache = open('/tmp/jobs/%s-cache.txt' % name).read().strip()
done = re.findall(r'SCRIPT DONE (\S+)', open('/tmp/jobs/%s-run.log' % name).read())[-1]
pieces = sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/%s.tar.[0-9]*' % piece))
free = subprocess.run("df -m / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}'", shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
status = subprocess.run('git status --porcelain | wc -l', shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd='/home/user/workspace/master').stdout.strip()
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
m = re.match(r'DROPPED with sudo at (\S+)', cache)
L = []
whole = piece.startswith('film-')
what = '%s, %s %s-%s' % (piece, seg, first, last) if whole else 'frames %s to %s of the piece film-16x9-final-b-%s, %s %s-%s' % (first, last, piece.split('-')[1], seg, first, last)
L.append('MAIL from handover_engineer to /root, %s UTC %s. JOB %s sent back (%s, on 262b9a68df0a6bda8d77518539580de554bb0dc5 in my clean tree /home/user/workspace/master).' % (now.strftime('%H:%M'), now.strftime('%d %b').lstrip('0'), name, what))
if len(pieces) == 1:
    L.append('Attached: %s (the only piece, %d bytes) and /tmp/%s-tail.txt.' % (pieces[0], os.path.getsize(pieces[0]), name))
else:
    L.append('Attached: %s and /tmp/%s-tail.txt.' % (', '.join('%s (%d bytes)' % (p, os.path.getsize(p)) for p in pieces), name))
if len(rcs) == 1:
    L.append('RC line, word for word: ' + rcs[0])
else:
    L.append('RC lines, word for word, in order: ' + ' / '.join(rcs))
L.append('Count of the first line of the tail: ' + tail[0])
if m:
    L.append('The cache: yes, done. sync; echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches ran with sudo at %s, before the build and the job.' % m.group(1))
else:
    L.append('The cache: NOT done: ' + cache)
L.append('Times: started %s, finished %s. The tool\'s line: %s. TIMES_NOTE' % (start, done, ' / '.join(wrote) if wrote else 'none'))
kept = sorted(glob.glob('/home/user/workspace/master/out/work/chunks/16x9-final-full/*.mp4'))
L.append('The files under out/work/chunks/16x9-final-full are kept (%d chunks with their json files, this one among them); git status of the tree shows %s; %s MB free. I wait for the next job.' % (len(kept), 'no change' if status == '0' else status + ' CHANGED LINES', free))
out = '\n'.join(L) + '\n'
open('/tmp/mail/%s-return.out' % name, 'w').write(out)
print('--- draft /tmp/mail/%s-return.out' % name)
print(out)
```

### `/tmp/jobs/alive.py` (4484 bytes, 75 lines)

```
# alive.py NAME SEGMENT FIRST LAST START_ISO [WINDOW_S] : prints the line owed to /root while a job with very slow frames runs and
# the mail asks to say whether the drawing process is alive and how long it has run. The drawing process is the gpu process of the
# tool's browser (it draws in software). Measured: the pids (ps), the age of the gpu process, its processor time, and the processor
# time it used in a window of WINDOW_S seconds (default 30) taken now; the rows of the job in out/work/looks/log.jsonl; the error
# lines and RC lines of the tool's log. Exit 1 when the state is not the plain one (no gpu process, no tool, the script finished,
# an error line): then write the line by hand. Each call adds a row to /tmp/jobs/NAME-alive.txt.
import subprocess, sys, time, datetime, re, json
name, seg, first, last, start = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4]), sys.argv[5]
win = int(sys.argv[6]) if len(sys.argv) > 6 else 30
t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(start)

def procs():
    out = subprocess.run(['ps', '-eo', 'pid,etimes,cputimes,args'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split('\n')[1:]
    res = []
    for l in out:
        p = l.split(None, 3)
        if len(p) == 4:
            res.append((int(p[0]), int(p[1]), int(p[2]), p[3]))
    tool = [p for p in res if 'tools/film.ts' in p[3] and 'preflight.cjs' in p[3]]
    gpu = [p for p in res if '--type=gpu-process' in p[3] and 'ms-playwright' in p[3]]
    return tool, gpu

tool1, gpu1 = procs()
time.sleep(win)
tool2, gpu2 = procs()
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
ran = int((now - t0).total_seconds() // 60)
log = open('/tmp/%s-log.txt' % name, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
bad = len(re.findall(r'Shader Error|not usable|FAILED|lost', log))
rcs = [l for l in log.split('\n') if l.startswith('RC film')]
try:
    done = 'SCRIPT DONE' in open('/tmp/jobs/%s-run.log' % name).read()
except Exception:
    done = False
rows = {}
for l in open('/home/user/workspace/master/out/work/looks/log.jsonl'):
    try:
        r = json.loads(l)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if r.get('segment') == seg and r.get('job') == 'film' and r.get('frame') is not None and first <= r['frame'] <= last:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(r['time'][:19])
        if t >= t0:
            rows.setdefault(r['frame'], t)
total = last - first + 1
head = 'handover_engineer on JOB %s, %s UTC %s: ' % (name, now.strftime('%H:%M'), now.strftime('%d %b').lstrip('0'))
plain = True
if gpu2 and tool2:
    g = gpu2[0]
    same = [p for p in gpu1 if p[0] == g[0]]
    used = g[2] - same[0][2] if same else None
    body = 'the drawing process is alive. The job has run %d minutes since its start at %s' % (ran, t0.strftime('%H:%M:%S'))
    body += ' (%s)' % ('the first run of the loop, no RC line in the log' if not rcs else 'run %d of the loop, the RC lines so far: %s' % (len(rcs) + 1, ' / '.join(rcs)))
    body += '. The film tool is pid %d; the drawing process (the gpu process of its browser, pid %d) is %d minutes old and has used %d minutes of processor time' % (tool2[0][0], g[0], g[1] // 60, g[2] // 60)
    if used is None:
        body += ' (it is a new process, started within the last %d s)' % win
        plain = False
    else:
        body += ', %d s of it in the %d s before this line' % (used, win)
        if used < win // 2:
            plain = False
    body += '. '
else:
    body = 'the drawing process is NOT alive (film tool processes: %d, gpu processes of its browser: %d), %d minutes after the start at %s. ' % (len(tool2), len(gpu2), ran, t0.strftime('%H:%M:%S'))
    plain = False
if total == 1:
    body += ('Frame %d is not finished yet (no row of this job in out/work/looks/log.jsonl). ' % first) if not rows else ('Frame %d is finished (its row in out/work/looks/log.jsonl at %s). ' % (first, rows[first].strftime('%H:%M:%S')))
else:
    body += '%d of %d frames finished (rows of this job in out/work/looks/log.jsonl). ' % (len(rows), total)
tail = 'No error line in the log.' if not bad else '%d ERROR LINES in the log.' % bad
print(head + body + tail)
open('/tmp/jobs/%s-alive.txt' % name, 'a').write('%s tool %s gpu %s rows %d rc %d bad %d\n' % (now.strftime('%H:%M:%S'), [(p[0], p[1], p[2]) for p in tool2], [(p[0], p[1], p[2]) for p in gpu2], len(rows), len(rcs), bad))
if done or bad or not plain:
    sys.stderr.write('NOT PLAIN: done %s bad %d plain %s\n' % (done, bad, plain))
    sys.exit(1)
```

### `/tmp/jobs/mkpackreturn.py` (5774 bytes, 75 lines)

```
# mkpackreturn.py NAME PIECE : for a finished PACK job (one picture of a pack, like im9-23): prints the facts and writes the draft
# of the return to /tmp/mail/NAME-return.out. NAME is the job (im9-42), PIECE the tar's base name under /tmp (r60-mercury-rise-k).
# Reads /tmp/jobs/NAME.sh (round, part, frames), /tmp/NAME.log (the RC line, the picture file, the tool's line), the tar and its
# pieces, the start, cache and run files of the job. If the pack's code is not 0 the draft says so and names the tail alone.
import sys, os, re, glob, subprocess, datetime
name, piece = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
tree = '/home/user/workspace/master'
script = open('/tmp/jobs/%s.sh' % name).read()
rnd = re.search(r'--round (\d+)', script).group(1)
part = re.search(r'--only (\S+)', script).group(1)
fa, fb = re.search(r'--frames (\d+)-(\d+)', script).groups()
log = open('/tmp/%s.log' % name, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read().split('\n')
rcs = [l for l in log if l.startswith('RC pack')]
pics = [l.strip() for l in log if l.strip().startswith('/') and l.strip().endswith('.png')]
tool = [l for l in log if l.startswith('pack round')]
bad = [l for l in log if re.search(r'Shader Error|not usable|FAILED|lost', l)]
start = open('/tmp/jobs/%s-start.txt' % name).read().strip()
cache = open('/tmp/jobs/%s-cache.txt' % name).read().strip()
done = re.findall(r'SCRIPT DONE (\S+)', open('/tmp/jobs/%s-run.log' % name).read())
pieces = sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/%s.tar.[0-9]*' % piece))
listing = subprocess.run(['tar', '-tvf', '/tmp/%s.tar' % piece], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip().split('\n')
files = {}
for l in listing:
    p = l.split()
    if len(p) >= 6 and not p[0].startswith('d'):
        files[p[5]] = int(p[2])
free = subprocess.run("df -m / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}'", shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
status = subprocess.run('git status --porcelain | wc -l', shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=tree).stdout.strip()
head = subprocess.run('git rev-parse HEAD', shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=tree).stdout.strip()
chunks = len(glob.glob(tree + '/out/work/chunks/16x9-final-full/*.mp4'))
tail_lines = open('/tmp/%s-tail.txt' % name, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read().count('\n')
print('--- log: %d lines; RC lines %s; picture lines %s; tool lines %s; error lines %d' % (len(log), rcs, pics, tool, len(bad)))
print('--- tail: %d lines' % tail_lines)
print('--- pieces: %s' % [(p, os.path.getsize(p)) for p in pieces])
print('--- tar:'); print('\n'.join(listing))
print('--- sha: %s' % subprocess.run('sha256sum /tmp/%s.tar.[0-9]* | cut -c1-110' % piece, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip())
print('--- start %s, done %s, cache: %s' % (start, done, cache))
print('--- HEAD %s, git status lines %s, free %s MB, chunks kept %d, running %s' % (head, status, free, chunks, subprocess.run("pgrep -f 'tools/(film|pack|still)' | wc -l", shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()))
code = rcs[-1].split()[-1] if rcs else 'NONE'
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
m = re.match(r'DROPPED with sudo at (\S+)', cache)
frames = 'frame %s' % fa if fa == fb else 'frames %s to %s' % (fa, fb)
L = []
L.append('MAIL from handover_engineer to /root, %s UTC %s. JOB %s sent back (%s of the part %s of the pack of round %s, on 262b9a68df0a6bda8d77518539580de554bb0dc5 in my clean tree /home/user/workspace/master).' % (now.strftime('%H:%M'), now.strftime('%d %b').lstrip('0'), name, frames, part, rnd))
ok = code == '0' and len(rcs) == 1 and len(pics) >= 1 and len(done) == 1 and pieces and not bad
if code == '0':
    if len(pieces) == 1:
        L.append('Attached: %s (the only piece, %d bytes, named as the split line wrote it) and /tmp/%s-tail.txt.' % (pieces[0], os.path.getsize(pieces[0]), name))
    else:
        L.append('Attached: %s (named as the split line wrote them) and /tmp/%s-tail.txt.' % (', '.join('%s (%d bytes)' % (p, os.path.getsize(p)) for p in pieces), name))
    L.append('Exit code of the pack: 0. The log\'s line, word for word: %s' % ' / '.join(rcs))
else:
    L.append('Attached: /tmp/%s-tail.txt ALONE, as the mail says for a code other than 0.' % name)
    L.append('THE PACK ENDED WITH A CODE OTHER THAN 0. The log\'s line, word for word: %s' % (' / '.join(rcs) if rcs else 'no RC line'))
for pic in pics:
    rel = pic.replace(tree + '/', '')
    if rel in files:
        j = files.get(rel + '.json')
        L.append('The picture file the log printed: %s (in the tar as %s, %d bytes%s).' % (pic, rel, files[rel], ', with its json, %d bytes' % j if j is not None else ', WITHOUT a json'))
    else:
        L.append('The picture file the log printed: %s (NOT in the tar).' % pic)
        ok = False
if not pics:
    L.append('The log printed NO picture file.')
if m:
    L.append('The cache: yes, done. sync; echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches ran with sudo at %s, before the build and the job.' % m.group(1))
else:
    L.append('The cache: NOT done: ' + cache)
L.append('Times: started %s, finished %s. The tool\'s line: %s' % (start, done[-1] if done else 'NOT FINISHED', ' / '.join(tool) if tool else 'none'))
L.append('The folder out/work/packs/.cache/round-%03d holds the picture of this job only (the first line of the script removed what stood there, as written); the %d chunks under out/work/chunks/16x9-final-full are kept with their json files; git status of the tree shows %s; %s MB free. I wait for the next job.' % (int(rnd), chunks, 'no change' if status == '0' else status + ' CHANGED LINES', free))
out = '\n'.join(L) + '\n'
open('/tmp/mail/%s-return.out' % name, 'w').write(out)
print('--- draft /tmp/mail/%s-return.out (%s)' % (name, 'plain' if ok else 'NOT PLAIN, READ IT'))
print(out)
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
```
